library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Rizk_2018_relebactam"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Rizk_2018_relebactam"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1128/AAC.01411-17>

Rizk and colleagues measured relebactam and imipenem in plasma, epithelial
lining fluid (ELF) and alveolar cells (AC) of healthy volunteers who received
five 30-minute infusions of relebactam 250 mg with imipenem-cilastatin 500 mg
every 6 hours, followed by one bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL)
per subject at 0.5, 1, 1.5 or 3 h after the last dose. Alongside a
noncompartmental analysis of the mean profiles, they fitted a population PK
model for relebactam only (imipenem lung penetration was modelled in a separate
publication, reference 21 of the paper).

Plasma disposition is a two-compartment model with linear clearance (Methods
Eq. 1-2). Of the three ELF approaches the authors compared (a third,
exchanging compartment; a time-invariant partition coefficient; an effect
compartment), the partition coefficient fitted best. The ELF concentration is
therefore algebraic (Eq. 3):

```
C_ELF = kELF * fu,REL * A1 / V1
```

with `kELF = 0.553` estimated and the unbound fraction in plasma `fu,REL`
fixed at 0.8; ELF drug is taken as 100% unbound. The fit used a naive pooled
approach, so the model has no between-subject variability: all variability is
residual. The packaged model has two ODE states and two outputs: total plasma
`Cc` and ELF `Celf` (both mg/L). The unbound plasma concentration is returned as
`Cu`.

# Population

```{r population}
mod_fun <- readModelDb("Rizk_2018_relebactam")
str(rxode2::rxode(mod_fun)$population)
```

Seventeen healthy subjects (14 male, 3 female) aged 24-42 years entered the
study; 16 completed it and form the per-protocol PK population (Results, first
paragraph). Eligibility required age 18-45 years, BMI at most 32 kg/m^2 and
creatinine clearance of at least 80 mL/min (Materials and Methods). Body weight
is not reported and the model has no covariates, so the virtual population needs
no covariate columns.

# Source trace

| Element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: 2 compartments, IV infusion | -- | Methods Eq. 1-2 |
| ELF partition on unbound plasma concentration | -- | Methods Eq. 3 |
| `lcl` | log(9.17 L/h) | Table 4 (thetaCL) |
| `lvc` | log(15.3 L) | Table 4 (thetaVc) |
| `lvp` | log(10.6 L) | Table 4 (thetaVp) |
| `lq` | log(2.64 L/h) | Table 4 (thetaQ2) |
| `lfelf` | log(0.553) | Table 4 (thetakELF) |
| `fu` | 0.8 (fixed) | Methods after Eq. 3 ('~80%'); Results ('80% unbound') |
| ELF unbound fraction | 1 (implicit) | Methods ('free fraction in the ELF was assumed to be 100%') |
| `addSd` | 0.01 mg/L (fixed) | Table 4 (sigma addi) |
| `propSd` | 0.28 | Table 4 (sigma prop, 28.0% CV) |
| `propSd_Celf` | 0.392 | Table 4 (sigma prop,kELF, 39.2% CV) |
| Dosing | 250 mg IV over 0.5 h every 6 h x 5 | Abstract; Materials and Methods |

# Typical-value checks

```{r typical, warning = FALSE}
mod <- rxode2::rxode(mod_fun)
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

dose_times <- (0:4) * 6
last_dose <- 24
dose_rows <- data.frame(
  id = 1L, time = dose_times, evid = 1L, amt = 250, dur = 0.5,
  cmt = "central", dvid = NA_integer_
)
obs_grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 30, by = 0.01), last_dose + c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 3))))
ev_typ <- bind_rows(
  dose_rows,
  data.frame(
    id = 1L, time = obs_grid, evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, dur = NA_real_,
    cmt = "central", dvid = 1L
  )
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim_typ <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_typ, useLinCmt = FALSE)) |>
  mutate(tad = time - last_dose)

# Linear disposition: AUC over the fifth dosing interval must equal Dose / CL.
tau <- filter(sim_typ, time >= last_dose, time <= last_dose + 6)
auc_tau <- sum(diff(tau$time) * (head(tau$Cc, -1) + tail(tau$Cc, -1)) / 2)
# The ELF:total plasma ratio is time-invariant, kELF * fu.
elf_ratio <- with(filter(sim_typ, Cc > 0), Celf / Cc)

c(auc_tau = auc_tau, dose_over_cl = 250 / 9.17, elf_ratio_min = min(elf_ratio), elf_ratio_max = max(elf_ratio))
stopifnot(
  abs(auc_tau / (250 / 9.17) - 1) < 0.002,
  all(abs(elf_ratio - 0.553 * 0.8) < 1e-8)
)
```

The model's own diagnostic figure (Figure 4, top left) draws the population
prediction for the fifth dose in mg/L. Its values at the peak and at 3 h, read
from the figure by the maintainers, are compared with the typical-value solve.

```{r fig4-pred}
fig4 <- data.frame(
  matrix = c("Plasma", "Plasma", "Plasma", "ELF", "ELF"),
  tad = c(0, 0.5, 3, 0.5, 3),
  pred_fig4 = c(1.0, 14.7, 3.0, 6.4, 1.35)
)
typ_at <- sim_typ |>
  filter(round(tad, 2) %in% fig4$tad) |>
  distinct(tad, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(tad, Plasma = Cc, ELF = Celf) |>
  pivot_longer(-tad, names_to = "matrix", values_to = "pred_model")
fig4_cmp <- inner_join(fig4, typ_at, by = c("matrix", "tad")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (pred_model / pred_fig4 - 1))
fig4_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Matrix = matrix, "Time after last dose (h)" = tad,
    "Figure 4 PRED (mg/L)" = pred_fig4, "Model (mg/L)" = pred_model, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Typical-value prediction against the PRED curves of Rizk 2018 Figure 4 (read from the figure).")
# The peak and 3-h values are read from a 0-20 mg/L axis; the trough at 1 mg/L
# is too close to the axis to read better than about 20%.
stopifnot(all(abs(fig4_cmp$pct_diff[fig4_cmp$tad > 0]) < 10))
```

# Simulation with residual error

Because the fit was naive pooled, a simulated cohort differs from the typical
profile only by residual error. 200 virtual subjects are sampled at the study's
nominal BAL times (0.5, 1, 1.5 and 3 h after the fifth dose) and at the pre-dose
trough. (rxode2 warns that the model has no omega parameters; that is expected
here and the warning is suppressed.)

```{r sim, warning = FALSE}
n_sub <- 200
samp <- last_dose + c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 3)
events <- bind_rows(
  lapply(seq_len(n_sub), function(i) {
    bind_rows(
      mutate(dose_rows, id = i),
      data.frame(
        id = i, time = rep(samp, 2), evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, dur = NA_real_,
        cmt = "central", dvid = rep(1:2, each = length(samp))
      )
    )
  })
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20180301)
sim <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events, useLinCmt = FALSE)) |>
  mutate(
    tad = round(time - last_dose, 2),
    matrix = ifelse(CMT == min(CMT), "Plasma", "ELF")
  )
```

# Replicating Figure 1 and Table 3

Figure 1 plots mean relebactam concentrations in micromolar. The model works in
mg/L; concentrations are converted with the relebactam molecular weight of
348.4 g/mol (C12H20N4O6S). The paper does not print the molecular weight, but
its mass-spectrometric transition (m/z 349, the protonated molecule) and the
four 0.5-h plasma observations of Figure 4 (mean about 16.7 mg/L against the
47.9 micromolar of Table 2) both agree with it.

```{r fig1, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 1 (bottom) of Rizk 2018: relebactam in plasma and ELF after the fifth dose. Lines: typical-value prediction; ribbons: 5th-95th percentiles of 200 simulated observations with residual error; points: published means (plasma Cmax from Table 2, ELF geometric means from Table 3)."}
mw <- 348.4
to_um <- function(x) x / mw * 1000

typ_long <- sim_typ |>
  filter(tad >= 0, tad <= 3) |>
  select(tad, Plasma = Cc, ELF = Celf) |>
  pivot_longer(-tad, names_to = "matrix", values_to = "conc") |>
  mutate(conc_um = to_um(conc))

pi_sim <- sim |>
  group_by(matrix, tad) |>
  summarise(
    lo = to_um(quantile(sim, 0.05)), hi = to_um(quantile(sim, 0.95)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

published <- data.frame(
  matrix = c("Plasma", rep("ELF", 4)),
  tad = c(0.5, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 3),
  conc_um = c(47.9, 14.93, 10.93, 9.49, 4.27)
)

ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = pi_sim, aes(tad, ymin = pmax(lo, 0.1), ymax = hi, fill = matrix), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(data = typ_long, aes(tad, conc_um, colour = matrix)) +
  geom_point(data = published, aes(tad, conc_um, colour = matrix), size = 2.5) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after last dose (h)", y = "Relebactam (micromolar)",
    colour = NULL, fill = NULL
  )
```

Table 1 of the paper reports ELF:plasma geometric-mean concentration ratios of
0.32 to 0.51 across the four BAL times. Under the partition model the ratio of
ELF to total plasma concentration is the constant `kELF * fu` = 0.442 at every
time, which sits within that range; the paper attributes the agreement of this
value (0.553 on an unbound basis) with the AUC-based penetration of 53.7% to the
rapid, hysteresis-free equilibration of ELF with plasma.

```{r table3}
table3 <- data.frame(tad = c(0.5, 1, 1.5, 3), gm_pub = c(14.93, 10.93, 9.49, 4.27))
elf_typ <- typ_long |>
  filter(matrix == "ELF", round(tad, 2) %in% table3$tad) |>
  distinct(tad, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(tad, conc_um)
table3_cmp <- inner_join(table3, elf_typ, by = "tad") |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (conc_um / gm_pub - 1))
table3_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Time after last dose (h)" = tad, "Table 3 ELF GM (micromolar)" = gm_pub,
    "Model typical value (micromolar)" = conc_um, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Typical ELF concentration against the geometric means of Rizk 2018 Table 3 (4 subjects per time).")
```

The typical value runs about 20% above the observed geometric means at 0.5 and
1 h and within 10% of them at 1.5 and 3 h. The model's own population prediction
does the same in Figure 4, where three of the four 0.5-h ELF observations lie
below the red PRED curve; the ELF residual error is 39% and each mean rests on
four subjects.

```{r table3-check}
stopifnot(
  # A transcription error in kELF, fu, CL or Vc moves every row by tens of percent.
  abs(median(table3_cmp$pct_diff)) < 20
)
```

# PKNCA: mean-profile NCA after the fifth dose

The paper's NCA (Table 2) was run in Phoenix on the mean concentration at each
nominal time, using the profile after the fifth dose. The same design is
applied to the typical-value prediction: PKNCA runs on the pre-dose trough and
the four BAL times, with time re-based to the last dose and the linear-up /
log-down trapezoidal rule.

```{r pknca}
conc_nca <- sim_typ |>
  filter(round(tad, 2) %in% c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 3)) |>
  distinct(tad, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(tad, Plasma = Cc, ELF = Celf) |>
  pivot_longer(-tad, names_to = "matrix", values_to = "conc") |>
  mutate(id = 1L, conc = to_um(conc), time = tad) |>
  filter(!is.na(conc)) |>
  select(id, matrix, time, conc)

dose_nca <- data.frame(id = 1L, matrix = c("Plasma", "ELF"), time = 0, amt = 250)

intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = c(3, Inf),
  auclast = c(TRUE, FALSE), cmax = c(TRUE, FALSE), tmax = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  aucinf.obs = c(FALSE, TRUE), half.life = c(FALSE, TRUE)
)

nca <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(
  PKNCAconc(conc_nca, conc ~ time | matrix + id),
  PKNCAdose(dose_nca, amt ~ time | matrix + id),
  intervals = intervals,
  options = list(auc.method = "lin up/log down")
))

nca_res <- as.data.frame(nca$result)

table2 <- data.frame(
  matrix = c("Plasma", "ELF"),
  aucinf.obs = c(81.2, 34.9),
  auclast = c(64.7, 26.7),
  cmax = c(47.9, 15.3),
  tmax = c(0.5, 0.5),
  half.life = c(1.24, 1.29)
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated     = nca_res,
  reference     = table2,
  by            = "matrix",
  params        = c("aucinf.obs", "auclast", "cmax", "tmax", "half.life"),
  units         = c(
    aucinf.obs = "micromolar*h", auclast = "micromolar*h",
    cmax = "micromolar", tmax = "h", half.life = "h"
  ),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Typical-value NCA after the fifth dose against Rizk 2018 Table 2 (mean-profile NCA). * differs by >20%.")
```

```{r nca-check}
auc_rows <- nca_res |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("aucinf.obs", "auclast")) |>
  select(matrix, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  inner_join(
    pivot_longer(table2, -matrix, names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "pub"),
    by = c("matrix", "PPTESTCD")
  ) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (PPORRES / pub - 1))
auc_rows
stopifnot(
  # Exposure is set by CL (plasma) and kELF * fu (ELF); a transcription or unit
  # error in either shifts these AUCs by far more than 15%.
  all(abs(auc_rows$pct_diff) < 15)
)
```

The model reproduces the mean-profile AUCs in both matrices within 5%. The
model's plasma Cmax is 13% below the observed mean at 0.5 h and its ELF Cmax is
21% above it (the one starred row), which mirrors the population prediction
against the observations in Figure 4: the model was not refitted, and these are
the published estimates. The terminal half-lives are 5-9% shorter than the
paper's NCA values from the observed means.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Imipenem not included.** The paper reports NCA for imipenem but fits a
  population model only for relebactam; imipenem lung penetration from this
  study was modelled in a separate publication (reference 21 of the paper).
* **Alveolar cells not modelled.** AC concentrations entered the NCA (Table 2)
  but not the population model.
* **Naive pooled fit.** The authors pooled the data without random effects, so
  the model carries no IIV; between-subject variability is absorbed into the
  residual error. Stochastic simulations therefore spread only by residual
  error.
* **Residual error scale.** Table 4 reports the proportional errors as percent
  CV (28.0% plasma, 39.2% ELF); they are encoded as proportional standard
  deviations 0.28 and 0.392. The additive plasma error of 0.01 mg/L was fixed
  by the authors.
* **Molecular weight.** Concentrations are compared in micromolar using
  348.4 g/mol, which the paper does not print (see Figure 1 section for the
  in-paper corroboration).
* **Figure 4 values.** The population-prediction values in the Figure 4 check
  were read from the figure by the maintainers and carry the precision of a
  visual read.
* **Unbound fraction.** The paper gives the relebactam unbound fraction in
  plasma as approximately 80% in the Methods and as 80% in the Results; 0.8 is
  used. The text after Eq. 3 labels it `fu,ELF` while the equation writes
  `fu,REL`; the description ('free fraction of relebactam in plasma') matches
  the equation.
* **Literature check.** No erratum or correction for this article was found in
  Europe PMC (checked 2026-11-25).
